verdicts.behavior: MSBuild CodeTaskFactory compiles a local interactive PowerShell host. Execute queries Windows version; versions above 6.3 decode Base64, decrypt a PowerShell AES SecureString using bytes 212 down to 181 as the key, and evaluate the plaintext. That plaintext sets AmsiUtils.amsiInitFailed to true. InitialSessionState is assigned the permissive base AuthorizationManager. Console input reaches AddScript/Invoke. HostUtilities reads registry/profile files; CredUI prompts return user-supplied credentials to requested PowerShell commands.
verdicts.judgment: Automatic, concealed AMSI disabling and deliberate command-policy bypass tip the judgment to likely malicious when found without authorization context. The disclosed BSD source and local interactive UI also fit authorized offensive research. Publication is not proof of hostile deployment; no deployment authorization is supplied.
verdicts.coverage: Two suspicious traits cover distinct supported concealment and policy-bypass behaviors. The engine recovers the Base64 layer but does not decrypt the keyed AES blob; its AMSI field write is a manual finding. No remote command channel, credential theft, injection or persistence is inferred from the host boilerplate.

verdicts.behavior: An Add event records a parent-path auto-script object targeting Apache configuration outside its normal storage area. The supplied mod_md configuration chooses DNS-01 with /bin/node as the challenge command, an external-IP ACME authority, and always-on renewal. It is an attack-bearing configuration record, not a program executed by reading the log.
verdicts.judgment: Traversal into Apache configuration combined with the interpreter renewal hook supports deliberate exploitation/persistence rather than normal certificate administration. This artifact alone does not establish a planted setup script, appliance version, successful invocation, or administrator authorization.
verdicts.coverage: One hostile renewal-hook finding plus three suspicious traversal/hook findings. A second distinct hostile behavior is not established by this audit record; no duplicate hostile rule was invented to meet a count.

verdicts.identification: Python SSH deployer for a FortiOS auto-script/Apache challenge chain
verdicts.behavior: At module load subprocess.run sends the raw configuration through SSH stdin to admin@firewall.example. Commands kill miglogd/syslogd and clear crash logs, write a traversing setup script and Apache mod_md configuration. The Node setup script downloads a first JS stage, runs it, unlinks it on process close; nested downloads stage JS, WASM and another payload, then wait 180 seconds before launching Node with staged file paths. The DNS challenge hook supplies recurring activation.
verdicts.judgment: Logging blackout, escaped configuration writes and linked remote-code activation demonstrate attack purpose. The placeholder SSH host makes this a deployer template requiring a reachable target and credentials; authorization, vulnerable appliance version and final stage contents remain unknown.
verdicts.coverage: All three hostile and four suspicious findings retained. Timer use is not labeled analysis evasion; the unknown downloaded payload is not assigned a malware family.

rule_changes.change: Retired its broad disjunction. An unconditional loop, a download reference, a namespace or an allocation API alone does not establish payload activation. Normal build-loop and PowerShell-host controls demonstrate the overclaim. Each supported observation survives in its canonical neutral trait.
rule_changes.retained_attack_coverage: Specific APC injection stays hostile. The public Empire MSBuild/WMI module retains both hostile execution findings. A GreatSCT-derived native allocation/copy/thread control receives a focused suspicious API-profile rule; references alone do not bind the buffer to the thread entry point.
